title: Transfection of O. marina using particle bombardment
author: Pia Elustondo
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ui7euhn
materials: Digest at least 10 ug of DNA for each transformation. Ideally cut near the 3' end of your gene of interest in the plasmid Clean up de digested DNA. We used QiaEx II (QIAGEN), but any method is acceptable.
Allow the particles to settle for 1 min

Biolistic PDS-1000/He Particle delivery system (Bio-Rad) a. Test the rupture disk with the highest pressure (no cells, no gold particles) b. Sterilize the rupture disks by soaking them in 70 % isopropanol just prior to insertion in the retaining cap. They are assembled and placed on the top of the biolistic system chamber. REMEMBER THE STOPPING SCREEN!!! c. Sterilize the target shelf by whipping it with 70 % EtOH and drying it in the sterilie flowhood d. Shooting parameters: for the 1100 psi rupture discs: Bring the Hg pressure to 25, press hold , fire. For the 1350 psi bring the Hg pressure to 27.5, press hold and fire. The switching should be very fast because the cells are subjected to vaccum before the rupture e. Shoot each plate twice, rotate the plate 90 degrees between each shot. f. After bombardment, the cells are checked under the microscope and F/2 complete media is added to the plateg. g. Selection antibiotic (Bleomycing 15 ug/ml or Puromycing 10 ug/ml) was added two days after the transfection to allow for recovery and protein synthesis.

Digest at least 10 ug of DNA for each transformation. Ideally cut near the 3' end of your gene of interest in the plasmid Clean up de digested DNA. We used QiaEx II (QIAGEN), but any method is acceptable.

steps.title: Concentrate O. marina cells
steps.instruction: Prepare concentrated pellets of O. marina while minimizing cell death from centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Incubate 4 x 50 ml tubes at 4 ºC for 30 min or at 16 ºC for 1-2 h to slow organism movement.
Centrifuge 2 tubes at a time for 10 min at 10 ºC and 500 g (keep remaining tubes in fridge or 16 ºC incubator).
Carefully discard the top 40 ml and combine the pellets.
Verify pellets under a microscope.

steps.title: Sterilize equipment and prepare reagents
steps.instruction: Sterilize necessary hardware and prepare stock solutions for the bombardment process.

substeps.instruction: Autoclave macrocarrier holders, stoppin screens, rupture disks, retaining caps, microcarrier launch assembly, and 2 ml Eppendorf tubes.
Prepare 1% agarose in F/2 plates.
Sterilize circular paper filter disks (4.25 cm) by placing them in Petri dishes and microwaving for 3 min in intervals of 1 min each, allowing them to cool between cycles.
Prepare sterile complete F/2 media.
Prepare 50% sterile glycerol.
Prepare 70% isopropanol.
Prepare 0.1 M spermidine (free base, tissue grade); may be aliquoted and stored at -20 ºC.
Prepare 2.5 M CaCl2; may be aliquoted and stored at -20 ºC.

steps.title: Prepare gold particle stock
steps.instruction: Prepare a 60 mg/ml gold particle suspension for storage at -20 ºC.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 20 mg of 0.6 um gold particles into a 1.5 ml sterile Eppendorf tube.
Add 1 ml of 70% Ethanol and vortex for 5 min.
Allow particles to soak in 70% Ethanol for 15 min.
Pellet particles by spinning for 5-10 s at high speed and discard supernatant.
Wash particles three times: add 1 ml sterile water, vortex 1 min, let settle for 1 min, pellet by briefly spinning, and discard fluid.
Re-suspend particles in 500 ul of 50% glycerol to reach a final concentration of 60 mg/ml.

steps.title: Prepare target plates
steps.instruction: Prepare the agarose plates and apply the cell culture.

substeps.instruction: Autoclave and pour very thin 1% agarose plates (0.25-0.5 cm) in F/2 media.
Apply one sterilized filter paper disk to each agarose plate.
Cover the disk with 500 ul of concentrated culture.

steps.title: Coat gold particles with DNA
steps.instruction: Prepare the DNA-gold particle complex for bombardment.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 25 μl of gold particle stock (60 mg/ml) into a 2 ml Eppendorf tube and vortex.
Add 2.5 - 5 μg of DNA while vortexing and continue vortexing for 3-5 min.
Carefully add 25 μl of 2.5 M CaCl2 and 10 μl of 0.1 M spermidine to the walls of the tube; mix on the walls and tilt the tube up while vortexing to prevent clumping.
Vortex for 3 min.
Incubate on ice for 1 min.
Spin for 10 s at full speed and discard the supernatant.
Add 70 μl of 70% Ethanol, re-suspend, vortex, spin down, and discard supernatant.
Add 70 μl of 100% Ethanol, re-suspend, vortex, spin down, and discard supernatant.
Re-suspend in 26 μl of 100% Ethanol by gently vortexing for 30 s.
In a cell culture hood, spread 12 μl on the center of each macrocarrier disc and allow to dry.
